instrument: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, Pub. L. 117-328, Division FF, §1262(a)(1)
quote: Section 1262(a)(1) of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 (Pub. L. No: 117-328), which was enacted on December 29, 2022, amended the CSA (21 U.S.C. 823(h)) by eliminating the requirement that practitioners obtain a waiver to prescribe certain schedule III--V medications for the treatment of opioid use disorder (OUD). This immediately removed the requirement for practitioners to submit a notification of intent and to receive the Drug Addiction Treatment Act of 2000 (DATA)-Waiver before prescribing buprenorphine.
note: Federal waiver eliminated immediately by statute; 89 FR 7528 at 7534 supplies authoritative effect/date explanation. DEA corroboration: https://www.deadiversion.usdoj.gov/pubs/docs/dear-registrant-AM-01122023.html — "A DATA-Waiver registration is no longer required to treat patients with buprenorphine for opioid use disorder." This does not repeal state laws or the ordinary DEA-registration requirement. The later Part 8 rule effective date is not the waiver-elimination date.

instrument: 21 CFR 1306.07(b), current eCFR; DEA 88 FR 53377 (2023)
quote: Nothing in this section shall prohibit a practitioner, who is not specifically registered to conduct a narcotic treatment program, from dispensing (but not prescribing) narcotic drugs, in accordance with applicable Federal, State, and local laws relating to controlled substances, to one person or for one person's use at one time for the purpose of initiating maintenance treatment or detoxification treatment (or both).
note: None-found under the expressly short-term-exception reading: current §1306.07(b) retains the no-prescription exception, a three-day limit and referral arrangement. The 2023 amendment adds dispensing of the full three-day supply at once; it does not withdraw administration permission. Independent Schedule III-V prescribing authority now appears in §1306.07(d), consistent with waiver elimination. Thus this is not a global ban on prescribing buprenorphine; if read as such, that overbroad reading conflicts with the 2022 waiver repeal. Checked actual current eCFR text in Neo, current through 2026-10-22; webtext extraction returned only navigation.

instrument: 21 CFR 1306.07(c), current eCFR
quote: This section is not intended to impose any limitations on a physician or authorized hospital staff to administer or dispense narcotic drugs in a hospital to maintain or detoxify a person as an incidental adjunct to medical or surgical treatment of conditions other than addiction, or to administer or dispense narcotic drugs to persons with intractable pain in which no relief or cure is possible or none has been found after reasonable efforts.
note: None-found: current eCFR retains the hospital incidental-adjunct exception. The 2023 three-day dispensing amendment is paragraph (b); it does not impose a three-day cap on paragraph (c) hospital care for other medical conditions. The DATA-waiver elimination expands separate prescribing access rather than withdrawing hospital continuation.

instrument: DEA, Dispensing of Narcotic Drugs To Relieve Acute Withdrawal Symptoms of Opioid Use Disorder, 88 FR 53377, FR Doc 2023-16892, 21 CFR 1306.07(b)
quote: Not more than a three-day supply of such medication may be dispensed to the person or for the person's use at one time while arrangements are being made for referral for treatment.
note: Historical-report reading: the region expressly says "Previously", "Congress directed", and "DEA subsequently advised"; it reports the former one-day rule and interim DEA advice, not a present direction to request an exception. The 2023 final rule replaces that former procedure but does not falsify those historical events. If the region is instead treated as asserting a currently pending amendment/current exception-request requirement, that part is obsolete from 2023-08-08; evidence: "DATES: This final rule is effective on August 8, 2023." Correct citation = 88 FR 53377, not 88 FR 50043 (an unrelated CMS correction). The quoted operative sentence supplies the new three-day-at-once rule. No live recommendation is withdrawn on the historical reading.
